messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: KV cache mem-usage spike and OOMs in hosted-runtime-us-west-2. Alert group: kvcache.ooms.high. 65 hosts reporting >90% mem and repeated OOMs in last 3m.

ninesh (oncall): ack. I'm on it. any visible customer errors?

alice (sre): seeing 503s surfaced from proxy and a surge in stream failures. error rate for /v1/generate up ~3.2% overall, peaks ~12% for a small cohort.

bob (runtime): root cause looks like runaway context windows + continuous-prefetch growth. sessions with very long prompts are causing KV maps to balloon; prefetch windows keep extending due to our soft-condition for prefix-matching.

carla (ml-infra): adding that continuous batching kept merging very long requests into shared batches which amplified KV growth per shard. sequence length distribution skewed heavily >64k tokens for a few sessions.

incident-bot: Pager duty: @dinesh. Severity: P1. Runbook: kvcache-oom. Steps: reduce prefetch depth -> enable session caps -> apply emergency batch limiter.

dinesh (oncall): executing mitigation plan now. calling for runtime patch.

bob (runtime): proposing immediate hotfix: 1) force prefetch.window.max=4096 -> set to 512 2) max_prefetch_tokens_per_session=20000 -> set to 8000 3) continuous_batch.max_window_tokens=8192 -> set to 2048. This should limit KV growth and batch amplification.

alice (sre): rolling the config change to hosted runtime config-store (canary 10% then 100%). watching memory and 503s.

deploy-bot: Started rollout: config/hosted-runtime/us-west-2 -> canary=10% by alice. ID: cfg-roll-5501234567

bob (runtime): sharing quick curl for emergency toggle if needed:

```
curl -X POST https://config.internal.redwood/api/v1/flags/update \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"service":"hosted-runtime","env":"us-west-2","changes": {"prefetch.window.max":512,"max_prefetch_tokens_per_session":8000,"continuous_batch.max_window_tokens":2048}}'
```

carla (ml-infra): Ran prom query: sum(rate(kvcache_entries_added_total[5m])) by (shard) shows a 6x increase vs baseline on 12 shards. mem_used_bytes per shard peaked at 94% on shard-7.

alice (sre): canary looks good after 3m: shard mem usage trending down ~18% on canary hosts. error rate on canary customers down to ~0.5%. expanding rollout.

eva (support): collecting impacted customers list from error-traces. two customers (cust-phi and cust-xyz) saw higher rates and raised support tickets. ETA for clear?

bob (runtime): ETA for broad rollout completion ~8m. after full rollout we'll also enable a temporary per-request token cap at the proxy layer: 120k tokens for hosted-v1 endpoints to prevent single-session blowouts.

dinesh (oncall): implementing proxy cap now.

deploy-bot: Rollout completed to 100% in us-west-2. ID: cfg-roll-5501234567 status=SUCCESS by alice.

incident-bot: Automated remediation performed: config rollback disabled=false, prefetch.window.max=512, continuous_batch.max_window_tokens=2048.

alice (sre): monitoring: overall OOMs dropped to zero in the last 5m, 503s back to baseline (~0.1%). latency slightly elevated for some sessions while caches warm.

carla (ml-infra): note: we still see long-lived sessions with very high KV cardinality. recommend adding an eviction policy to trim stale prefixes after X tokens or time (e.g., evict prefix if not accessed in 15m).

bob (runtime): agreed. we'll prepare a more robust fix: switch from unbounded prefix prefetch to size-bounded sliding-window prefetch + per-session KV soft-cap. will patch in next maintenance release.

alice (sre): customer comms suggestion: update status.redwood.ai with short blurb that hosted API experienced elevated 503s due to runaway context windows; mitigated by config changes; no ongoing degradation. draft below:

"We experienced elevated errors on the hosted API caused by unusually long input contexts that triggered internal cache growth. We deployed an emergency configuration change to limit prefetch and batching while we prepare a permanent fix. Error rates have returned to normal — we continue to monitor."

eva (support): posted status update and pinged impacted customers with mitigation note and that we are investigating root cause.

dinesh (oncall): starting a 2hr post-mortem timer. will collect logs, heap/kv snapshots (sampled) and affected session IDs. handing over to day shift in 1h if stable. next oncall: alice (sre) at 12:00 UTC.

bob (runtime): quick dataset of useful commands for handoff:

```
# check kvcache mem per shard
promql: max by (shard) (avg_over_time(kvcache_mem_bytes[2m]))
# list top sessions by kv size
kdump: /internal/tools/top_kv_sessions --since 30m --limit 50
```

alice (sre): upload snapshots to /var/incidents/5501234567 and link in the postmortem.

incident-bot: Handoff checklist: incident stamped P1 -> mitigated config applied -> customer comms posted -> artifacts: heap-snapshots, prom-queries, session-ids -> assigned postmortem: runtime-team + ml-infra.

dinesh (oncall): happy with state. if we see re-escalation, page again. leaving this thread and moving to handoff. :white_check_mark:

alice (sre): taking over for follow-up. will open postmortem doc and assign action items (prefetch algorithm hard cap, sliding eviction, improved alerting on prefetch growth).
